gaps: Which RD(s) the customer means: how to identify and choose among multiple linked recurring deposits, and what to do if the customer gives an unlinked or ambiguous ID
Which lookup steps are required and in what order for 'status' (balance, installments paid, missed installments, maturity date, rate) and whether a status check alone is sufficient

Whether the closure quote is informational only or leads to actual closure; the customer may stop after the quote, change their mind, or confirm closure, and the policy gives no rule for when to proceed

What 'renewal change' means for an RD: auto-renewal on/off, maturity instruction change, or payout account change. Which tool or process applies, and whether it is supported or needs a service request

Premature closure rules: penalty, reduced interest rate, minimum tenure, treatment of missed installments, TDS, and loans against the RD, all of which come from the knowledge base and are not in the policy

Edge cases: RD already matured or closed, RD with an active lien or loan against it, RD near maturity where waiting may be better, and the simulation date (2026-07-16) affecting maturity and penalty calculations
Final action expected: close_deposit, renewal update, service request, or no mutation. What counts as explicit confirmation, and how to behave if the customer asks for advice on whether to close
Where closure proceeds are credited (which linked account), and whether the customer can choose the destination
Customer behavior: whether they compare quote versus keeping the RD, change their mind midway, or ask for the renewal change after seeing the quote, which affects the order of mutations
Bank conventions: how to present quote figures (gross vs. net, penalty breakdown), rounding, currency formatting, and when the KB must be searched again after weak hits
Escalation boundary: when an unsupported renewal change should become a service request versus a human transfer
